topics.title: How Did Ancient Humans Stay Clean Without Soap?
topics.notes: Ep 7 — PROMISED in Ep 6 (open loop + poster + recap): Greeks/Romans cleaned without soap — olive oil rubbed on, then scraped off with a strigil (curved metal scraper); poster hook: "No soap. Just oil and a metal scraper." Must feature this. Other ideas (verify): early soap-like recipes in Mesopotamian clay tablets (fat + ash); Egyptian natron; Roman public baths; prehistoric hygiene (Neanderthal toothpick grooves); hunter-gatherer hygiene today. Poster: COMING SOON. Make its Short too. DONE (applied expert fixes: cold open = poster promise, intro ≤15s, re-hooks). Facts: strigil/gloios (Beroea), lice 83–170k yrs (Toups 2011), Mohenjo-daro Great Bath, Egypt natron/Herodotus/tooth powder, Babylon 2800 BC, Roman thermae, Seneca 56, Mitchell 2016, fullonica + Vespasian, medieval stews, Vigarello linen, Aztec bathing. topics.title: How Did Ancient Humans Go to the Toilet?
topics.notes: Ep 8 — PROMISED in Ep 7 (open loop + poster + recap): Roman public latrines — rows of seats, no partitions; tersorium/xylospongium (sponge on a stick; Seneca Letter 70 mentions it; exact use debated — say so). Poster asks: before toilet paper, what did people use? Ideas (verify): Greek pessoi (ceramic pebbles, Charlier 2012 BMJ), Chinese toilet paper (6th c. Yan Zhitui; 14th c. imperial production), corncobs, moss/leaves; Mohenjo-daro toilets & drains; medieval garderobes; chamber pots; Neolithic latrine at Skara Brae?; coprolites as archaeology. Cold open must pay off the sponge promise. Poster: COMING SOON. Make its Short too. DONE: Roman latrines + tersorium (debated), pessoi (Charlier 2012), Xuanquanzhi sticks (Yeh & Mitchell 2016), Yan Zhitui + 1393 Ming paper, Gayetty 1857, Mohenjo-daro, Paisley Caves, Lloyds Bank coprolite, garderobes, Harington 1596, Cumming 1775, squatting (Sikirov 2003), BMJ 2007, JMP 2025.
